By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).
